description: NASA Space Apps Challengers là một đội ngũ đa ngành gồm các kỹ sư AI, nhà phân tích dữ liệu và nhà thiết kế toàn diện, cùng chung kết bởi một mục tiêu: biến dữ liệu mở của NASA thành những trải nghiệm rõ ràng, hữu ích và truyền cảm hứng.
summary: Mekong Challenger Project is an offline-first, field-centered decision-support web application designed to help farmers and agricultural extension officers in Vietnam's Mekong Delta plan resilient crop rotations. Addressing the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge, the platform combines NASA Terra MODIS (MOD13Q1) vegetation calendars, 25 years of NASA POWER daily agroclimatic records (2001–2025), and 22 environmental layers from NASA EOSDIS GIBS and ISRIC SoilGrids with on-farm soil pH, salinity, and irrigation inputs. Users can trace their field boundaries on an interactive map, evaluate crop suitability using FAO-56 water balance models and FAO agronomic thresholds, run drought and temperature stress tests, and compare three-season rotation strategies with transparent data provenance. Because smallholder farmers face severe dry-season water deficits, saline intrusion, and soil depletion from continuous rice monoculture, one failed harvest can jeopardize household livelihoods. By translating satellite observations into clear, bilingual, and offline-accessible guidance, Mekong Challenger Project supports local communities in making informed, sustainable farming decisions.
details:
Mekong Challenger is an offline-first, field-centered web application that helps smallholder farmers and agricultural extension officers in Vietnam's Mekong Delta evaluate land conditions and plan climate-resilient crop rotations. Users begin by locating their farm across the 13 Mekong Delta provinces and tracing their field boundaries on an interactive map, which calculates parcel area in hectares and square meters while checking for geometry errors. Users can explore 22 environmental layers at 5 km resolution covering terrain, water and flood dynamics, soil properties, and vegetation heat stress. When a farmer has not yet tested their soil, the system provides clearly labeled reference estimates from 5 km satellite and soil grids for pH, salinity, soil group, and seasonal timing, while immediately prioritizing any on-farm measurements entered by the user.

Using 25 years of daily NASA POWER agroclimatic data (2001–2025) and NASA Terra MODIS (MOD13Q1) crop calendars, our agronomic engine calculates FAO-56 Penman-Monteith reference evapotranspiration (ET0), FAO Manual 3 effective rainfall, and seasonal water balance (P - ET0). It evaluates nine crops using sourced thresholds from FAO-56, FAO-29, and FAO ECOCROP across three annual seasons, generating and comparing rotation strategies focused on balanced production, water conservation, and soil health restoration. Users can also adjust rainfall and temperature sliders to run what-if climate stress tests, replay historical drought years, and print an A4 PDF summary for field consultations.

The intended impact of the project is to reduce crop failure risk and water stress for farming communities facing dry-season drought, saline intrusion, and soil fatigue from continuous triple-rice monoculture. Rather than issuing automated commands, our platform is designed to compare options and explain the underlying evidence so that farmers and local extension officers can make informed decisions together.

Our project introduces several creative and practical design choices tailored to real rural conditions. First, we strictly separate hard physical eligibility constraints (such as severe soil acidity or salinity limits) from seasonal climate risks, preventing dangerous field conditions from being hidden inside an average score. Second, every number in the interface carries an explicit confidence rating (High for on-farm measurements, Medium for satellite observations, Reference for model grids, and Simulated for stress tests) and an interactive evidence ledger showing its exact data source and formula. We also deliberately excluded coarse 300 km GRACE gravity data from 5 km field assessments to prevent false precision. Third, our dual-tier AI assistant includes an offline rule-based fallback and a strict numerical verification filter that blocks any generated figure not grounded in the parcel's verified evidence ledger. Finally, we considered rural connectivity constraints by compiling the entire application, fonts, map library, and precomputed NASA datasets into a single self-contained 2.85 MB HTML file that runs offline in any browser without installation or login.

To build Mekong Challenger, we used JavaScript (ES Modules, Node.js), HTML5, Tailwind CSS v4, and Leaflet for interactive mapping and parcel geometry calculations. We used Python and Node.js pipelines to process NASA MODIS MOD13Q1, NASA POWER, NASA EOSDIS GIBS, SERVIR Mekong ESI, ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0, and FAO DSMW datasets. For the optional AI assistant and rotation brainstorming endpoint, we integrated the Google GenAI SDK (Gemini), and we validated our scientific formulas, data provenance, and complete Vietnamese/English bilingual localization with 204 automated unit tests.
